title: Eighth Word Religion And Worldly Life Choosing Between Two Roads

questions.question: What main subjects does the passage say a person can understand by listening to the comparison?
questions.answer: It says the comparison helps explain the world, the human soul, the importance of religion, why life becomes like a prison without true religion, and how calling on Allah and believing in His oneness save a person from darkness.

questions.question: What choice was placed before the two brothers at the fork in the road?
questions.answer: They had to choose between a path with rules, safety, and happiness and a path with fewer limits but danger and misery.

questions.question: How was the road on the right described?
questions.answer: It was described as having order and discipline, with some difficulty, but leading to safety and well-being.

questions.question: How was the road on the left described?
questions.answer: It was described as having freedom from restraint on the surface, but leading to harm and unhappiness.

questions.question: What does the brother with good character say before taking his road?
questions.answer: He says that he puts his trust in Allah.

questions.question: Why did the better brother choose the right-hand road?
questions.answer: He chose it because he had good character and accepted order and rules.

questions.question: Why did the other brother choose the left-hand road?
questions.answer: He chose it because he was morally careless and wanted a path without restrictions.

questions.question: Which brother is followed more closely in this part of the story, and why?
questions.answer: The brother on the left is followed so the reader can see that what looks easy at first can actually become difficult and heavy.

questions.question: What lesson about freedom and rules can be inferred from the two roads?
questions.answer: It suggests that freedom without guidance can harm a person, while living by right guidance brings safety and peace.

questions.question: How does this opening comparison connect religion to a person’s life?
questions.answer: It shows religion as a guide that brings order, protection, and happiness instead of confusion and misery.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the comparison at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: Its purpose is to help the reader understand big truths about human life, religion, and the condition of the soul.

questions.question: Who gives direction to the two brothers when the road divides?
questions.answer: A serious man at the split in the road gives them guidance.

questions.question: What warning is given about the left-hand road?
questions.answer: The warning is that its lack of limits hides danger and misery.

questions.question: What promise is given about the right-hand road?
questions.answer: The promise is that even though it requires obedience and effort, it brings safety and happiness.

questions.question: What does the response of the good brother show about his faith?
questions.answer: It shows that he trusts Allah and is willing to follow what is right.

questions.question: What does the response of the other brother show about his attitude?
questions.answer: It shows that he prefers ease and unrestricted living over discipline and wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage contrast appearance and reality?
questions.answer: It shows that the road that seems harder is actually better, while the road that seems easier is actually worse.

questions.question: What kind of person is the second brother described as being?
questions.answer: He is described as immoral, lazy, and drawn to comfort without responsibility.

questions.question: Why is the right road not presented as completely easy?
questions.answer: Because the passage teaches that the right path includes responsibility and self-control.

questions.question: What overall message about religion can be drawn from the brothers’ choices?
questions.answer: True religion guides a person to the better path, even when that path requires obedience and patience.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens to the world and human life if true religion is missing?
questions.answer: The world becomes like a prison, and human beings become deeply unhappy.

questions.question: Which two expressions are presented as keys to freeing the human spirit from darkness?
questions.answer: Calling on Allah and declaring that no god deserves worship except Allah.

questions.question: Why is a comparison used instead of giving only direct statements?
questions.answer: A comparison makes the lesson easier to picture and understand through a story.

questions.question: What did the two brothers ask the man at the fork in the road?
questions.answer: They asked which road was the better one.

questions.question: What did the man say was required on the road to the right?
questions.answer: He said a person had to follow law and order.

questions.question: What did the man say was found within the hardship of the right road?
questions.answer: He said there was security and happiness in it.

questions.question: What did the man say was hidden inside the freedom of the left road?
questions.answer: He said danger and misery were hidden in it.

questions.question: In what way did the good brother’s character affect his choice?
questions.answer: His good character led him to accept guidance, trust Allah, and choose the disciplined path.

questions.question: In what way did the other brother’s character affect his choice?
questions.answer: His bad habits and laziness led him to choose the unrestricted path.

questions.question: What important life lesson can a student learn from the brothers’ first decision?
questions.answer: A person should not choose a path only because it seems easier; he should choose what is right and safe in the sight of Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say can solve the mystery of this world?
questions.answer: Turning to Allah and affirming His oneness solve it.

questions.question: What does the passage say can rescue the human spirit from darkness?
questions.answer: Faith in Allah and calling on Him rescue the human spirit from darkness.

questions.question: How are the two roads different in terms of rules?
questions.answer: The right road has rules and order, while the left road has no restraint.

questions.question: How are the two roads different in terms of outcome?
questions.answer: The right road leads to safety and happiness, while the left road leads to danger and misery.

questions.question: What did the good brother do after hearing the explanation about the roads?
questions.answer: He trusted Allah, took the right path, and followed the rules there.

questions.question: What did the other brother do after hearing the same explanation?
questions.answer: He chose the left path because he wanted freedom from limits.

questions.question: What does this show about how two people can react to the same advice?
questions.answer: It shows that character and attitude shape whether a person accepts good guidance or rejects it.

questions.question: Why is the left road said to be only outwardly easy?
questions.answer: Because it looks comfortable at first, but it actually leads to heavy trouble.

questions.question: What role does trust in Allah play in the better brother’s decision?
questions.answer: It gives him confidence to choose the path of obedience and order.

questions.question: What warning does this passage give to young people about following every desire?
questions.answer: It warns that chasing unrestricted freedom can lead to harm, even if it first looks attractive.

questions.question: What four big ideas about human life and belief are named before the story begins?
questions.answer: The passage points to understanding the world, the human spirit, the value of religion, and the miserable state of people without true religion.

questions.question: How is religion presented in relation to human happiness?
questions.answer: Religion is shown as necessary for peace, meaning, and rescue from darkness.

questions.question: What scene begins the comparison in the story?
questions.answer: Two brothers are traveling together and arrive at a place where the road splits into two directions.

questions.question: What kind of person was standing at the fork in the road?
questions.answer: He was a serious and weighty person who gave them guidance.

questions.question: What was the good side of the right-hand road?
questions.answer: Its good side was that it led to safety and happiness.

questions.question: What was the bad side of the left-hand road?
questions.answer: Its bad side was that it led to danger and wretchedness.

questions.question: What personal quality especially marks the brother who chose the right road?
questions.answer: He is marked by good character.

questions.question: What personal quality especially marks the brother who chose the left road?
questions.answer: He is marked by immorality and laziness.

questions.question: Why is the left-hand brother’s situation described as seeming easy but truly burdensome?
questions.answer: Because a path without discipline may feel light at first, but it brings serious trouble later.

questions.question: What main moral truth does the beginning of the story teach?
questions.answer: Right guidance may require effort, but it protects a person, while careless freedom can ruin him.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the connection between Islam and truth before the story starts?
questions.answer: It teaches that Islam is the true religion before Allah and that belief in Allah is central to understanding life.

questions.question: Why does the passage begin with words about Allah before telling the comparison?
questions.answer: It begins that way to center the lesson on faith, Allah’s oneness, and His authority over human life.

questions.question: What question did the brothers ask at the fork in the road?
questions.answer: They asked which road was the good one.

questions.question: What answer were they given about the road on the right?
questions.answer: They were told it required discipline, but it contained safety and happiness.

questions.question: What answer were they given about the road on the left?
questions.answer: They were told it offered freedom from restraint, but it contained danger and misery.

questions.question: How did the good brother respond to this guidance in both words and action?
questions.answer: He expressed trust in Allah and then chose the ordered path.

questions.question: How did the other brother respond to the same guidance?
questions.answer: He ignored the warning and took the unrestrained path.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about a person who rejects good limits?
questions.answer: It suggests that such a person may think he is choosing comfort, but he is actually choosing harm.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the role of discipline in a Muslim’s life from this passage?
questions.answer: Discipline is part of the safe and successful path, not a burden without purpose.

questions.question: If you had to state the central lesson of this passage in one sentence, what would it be?
questions.answer: Trusting Allah and following the path of right guidance lead to real safety and happiness, while following desires without limits leads to misery.
